title: session-window-429-repro-scratchpad
content:
Purpose:
Quick scratchpad for reproducing and reasoning about an unusual 429/401 combo we've seen from user-facing clients that reuse ephemeral API keys inside long-lived streaming connections. Trying to capture commands tried, error snippets, session/window hypotheses, and next small experiments.

High-level symptom summary (observed 2025-03-10 -> 2025-03-22):
- Customer A: intermittent 429 bursts on a single session id despite low request rate per-second from their side.
- Same session sometimes returns 401 right after a 429; client retries with same key, then 401 persists for ~30s.
- Rate headers when present look noisy: sometimes RateLimit-Remaining is negative or missing.
- Errors concentrated during scheduled CI job that spins up ~60 short-lived ephemeral keys, each streaming a small (100–300 token) response.

Key questions / hypotheses:
1) Session-window counting vs per-key counting: are streaming connections billed per-chunk or per-connection? Could streaming chunking + window expiry cause mid-stream 429s?
2) Ephemeral keys: backend rotates or invalidates keys centrally, but clients keep using a cached token -> 401 spike after a rotation event.
3) Race in rate-limit lookup: auth cache TTL + rate-window sliding bucket update causes inconsistent Remaining values; concurrent requests can overdraw bucket and lead to negative remaining then 401 if auth invalidation kicks in.
4) Proxy/gateway mis-tagging: requests proxied through internal load balancer occasionally drop rate headers, confusing clients into naive retries.
5) Client behaviors (no jitter/backoff + immediate reconnect) amplify a small quota pressure into bursts.

Commands and sim repros tried so far:
1) Single-key sequential (control):
   curl -i -H "Authorization: Bearer sk.test.CONTROL" -X POST 
     https://api.redwood.internal/v1/responses -d '{"model":"xsmall","input":"hi"}'
   -> Expected: 200. Observed: 200, RateLimit-Remaining: 119

2) Concurrent short streaming using curl + --no-buffer (10 clients):
   seq 1 10 | xargs -n1 -P10 -I{} curl -s -N -H "Authorization: Bearer sk.test.CONTROL" 
     -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/stream -d '{"model":"xsmall","input":"stream test"}' &
   -> Observed: occasional 429 responses after ~30s from start. Header: Retry-After: 2

3) Mimic ephemeral keys churn (create 60 keys and use each once):
   for i in $(seq 1 60); do \ 
     KEY=\"sk.test.ephemeral_${i}\"; \ 
     curl -s -H "Authorization: Bearer $KEY" -X POST https://api.redwood.internal/v1/responses -d '{"model":"xsmall","input":"hello"}' &
   done; wait
   -> Observed: ~8% returned 401, ~22% returned 429. Failures cluster in 10s windows.

4) Repro with vegeta load (rate window effects):
   echo '{"method":"POST","url":"https://api.redwood.internal/v1/responses","body":"{\"model\":\"xsmall\",\"input\":\"test\"}","header":{"Authorization":"Bearer sk.test.CONTROL"}}' > target.json
   vegeta attack -rate=50 -duration=30s -targets=target.json | vegeta report
   -> Observed 429 tail starting at ~9s; server logs show bucket depletion for key sk.test.CONTROL at that time.

Server-side error snippets captured from gateway logs:
- [req=R1] 2025-03-18T15:02:11Z 429 rate_exceeded window=60s limit=120 remaining=0
- [req=R2] 2025-03-18T15:02:12Z 401 invalid_api_key key_id=ephemeral_42 reason=\"rotated\"
- [req=R3] 2025-03-18T15:02:12Z 429 rate_exceeded window=1m limit=120 remaining=-3
- [req=R4] 2025-03-18T15:02:45Z 200 stream_closed tokens=112

Notable observations from logs:
- The 401 for ephemeral_42 appears ~1s after remaining became negative.
- Several requests for the same session_id had different key_id values in auth logs (client rotated keys mid-flight).
- RateLimit-Reset times sometimes differ by 1–2 seconds between proxied requests (possible clock skew or inconsistent cache TTLs).

Small experiments to run next (quick, actionable):
A) Reproduce pure session-window behavior with single ephemeral key that streams a long response, measure token-based vs connection-based counts. Steps:
   - Create ephemeral key with 10s TTL (dev-only)
   - Start a streaming request that yields tokens every 200ms for 60s
   - Observe server rate headers and any mid-stream 429/401
B) Add jitter and exponential backoff in client harness to measure amplification factor. Compare immediate reconnect vs jittered reconnect.
C) Force clock skew on a test gateway (±3s) to see if Reset header mismatch increases 401/429 combos.
D) Flip off auth-cache at edge for a minute to test if cache staleness causes the 401s.

Data/logs to pull for deeper triage:
- Gateway request traces for request_ids R1..R20 around incident windows (include x-forwarded-for, upstream backend id).
- Auth service audit (key_issued_at, key_revoked_at, last_seen) for ephemeral keys in the batch.
- Rate limiter metrics: sliding-window counts, token-bucket state, bucket timestamps for affected keys.
- Client telemetry (if available): session_id, local clock, SDK version, reconnect/backoff logic.

Mitigation ideas (short-term):
- Ensure ephemeral key rotation is coordinated with client-side refresh: add a grace window where old keys remain valid for 60s after rotation.
- Stabilize and publish RateLimit headers consistently across proxies (ensure header passthrough).
- In client SDK: sticky-auth: prefer same key for a session where possible; add jittered reconnect with exponential backoff for 429s.
- Add server-side enforcement to cap instantaneous concurrent streams per key to avoid microbursts hitting sliding-window anomalies.

Draft note to CS/SE to request customer help:
- Ask Customer A for the exact timing of their CI job and list of ephemeral key ids (or at least counts per minute).
- Request a short SDK trace with timestamps and session ids so we can correlate.

Tentative timeline and owners:
- Maya: run streaming long-run repro (A) by 2025-03-27.
- Diego: pull auth-service audit + keys list by 2025-03-25.
- Priya: check gateway header passthrough and proxy TTL settings by 2025-03-24.

Other stray notes / quick wins that didn't pan out yet:
- Tried increasing per-key limit on a test cluster -> 429s moved to other keys, suggests global windowing behavior not single-key misconfig.
- Turning off streaming (convert to batched non-stream requests) dramatically reduces 429 frequency in the same load scenario -> streaming path has different accounting.

Open questions for infra/rl teams:
- Is the streaming path incrementing window counters on each chunk or on connection open/close? Need definitive code pointer.
- Are rate-limiter clock sources all synchronized (NTP)? Any documented skews on prod LB?
- What's policy for key rotation grace period for ephemeral keys?

If you pick this up: start with the streaming long-run repro and attach full gateway traces to the linear ticket INC-4321. Keep notes here and I'll prune into a more formal postmortem after we confirm root cause.

-- maya
